questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 9 cm. What is its total surface area? (Use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(4) + 2(3.14)(2)(9) = 25.1 + 113.0 = 138.2 cm². A common slip is forgetting the two circular ends (giving 113.0) or only using one end.

questions.subject: History
options: The Nazi government that ruled Germany from 1933
The German Empire under Kaiser Wilhelm before WWI
The Allied council that occupied Germany after WWII
questions.why: The Weimar Republic was Germany's first democracy, formed after the Kaiser abdicated in 1919, and it lasted until Hitler took power in 1933. Mixing it up with the Nazi era or the Kaiser's empire confuses the timeline of German history.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 13 cm and a height of 6 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 13 × 6 = 39 cm². The 78 cm² answer skips the halving step (just multiplying base × height) — that's the rushing mistake to keep guarding against, even though the concept itself is solid.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 6 cm and height 9 cm. What is its total surface area? (Use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(36) + 2(3.14)(6)(9) = 226.1 + 339.1 = 565.2 cm². Forgetting to double the circle area (only counting one end) gives the 339.1 cm² trap.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which one is FALSE about the Weimar Republic?
options: It was Germany's government from 1933 to 1945, led by Hitler
It used a system of proportional representation in parliament
It faced hyperinflation in 1923 that wrecked savings
It was formed in 1919 after Germany's defeat in WWI
questions.answer: It was Germany's government from 1933 to 1945, led by Hitler
questions.why: The Weimar Republic ended in 1933 when Hitler became Chancellor — the Nazi dictatorship that followed was a different regime, not the Weimar Republic itself. Confusing the two eras is the exact mix-up to watch for.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why the Great Depression specifically boosted support for the Nazi Party, rather than just making Germans generally unhappy?
options: Mass unemployment made the Nazis' promises of jobs and strong leadership seem like a real solution, unlike the struggling Weimar government
The Depression made every political party equally popular since everyone was suffering
The Depression only affected farmers, and the Nazis were mainly a farmers' party
The Depression happened after Hitler was already Chancellor, so it didn't affect his rise
questions.answer: Mass unemployment made the Nazis' promises of jobs and strong leadership seem like a real solution, unlike the struggling Weimar government
questions.why: The Nazis specifically gained because they offered decisive, confident solutions (jobs, national pride) while the Weimar government looked weak and divided — it's a causal link, not just coincidence in timing. Saying 'everyone got equally unhappy' misses that the Nazis uniquely benefited.
